question_text: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. You eat 1 slice. What fraction did you eat?
hint: Count the slices you ate (top) and the total slices (bottom).
worked_solution_steps: You ate 1 slice out of 4 total slices.
The top number (numerator) is how many you ate: 1
The bottom number (denominator) is how many slices there were: 4
analogy: The bottom number tells you how many pieces, and the top tells you how many you picked!

question_text: A chocolate bar has 6 equal pieces. You eat 2. What fraction did you eat?
hint: How many pieces did you eat? How many were there in total?
worked_solution_steps: You ate 2 pieces out of 6 total pieces.
analogy: Imagine the chocolate bar split into 6 squares — you grabbed 2 of them!

hint: Imagine sharing a cake — fewer people sharing means bigger pieces!
worked_solution_steps: 1/2 means the pizza is cut into 2 pieces — you get a big half!
1/4 means the pizza is cut into 4 pieces — each piece is smaller.
analogy: Sharing between 2 people gives you much more than sharing between 4!

hint: Sharing between 3 people gives bigger pieces than sharing between 5.
worked_solution_steps: 1/3 means split into 3 — each piece is quite big.
1/5 means split into 5 — each piece is smaller.
A bigger bottom number means smaller pieces!
analogy: If you share a cake with 3 friends, everyone gets more than if you share with 5!

hint: If you have half a pizza and get another half, how much do you have?
worked_solution_steps: The bottoms are the same (both 2), so just add the tops.
analogy: Half a pizza plus another half gives you a whole pizza!

question_text: A cake is cut into 3 equal slices. You eat 2 slices. What fraction did you eat?
hint: How many slices did you eat? How many slices was the cake cut into?
worked_solution_steps: You ate 2 slices out of 3 total.
analogy: You ate most of the cake — just one slice left!

hint: Try cutting each half into two — how many pieces do you have now?
worked_solution_steps: 1/2 means one out of two equal parts.
2/4 means two out of four equal parts.
If you cut each half into two, you get quarters — 2 of the 4 quarters is the same amount.
analogy: Same amount of pizza, just cut into smaller slices!

question_text: There are 8 sweets in a bag. You take 3. What fraction did you take?
hint: How many did you take (top) out of how many total (bottom)?
worked_solution_steps: You took 3 sweets out of 8 total.
analogy: 3 out of 8 sweets — you left 5 in the bag!

question_text: A football team has 5 players on the pitch. 2 of them score a goal. What fraction scored?
hint: How many scored (top) out of how many players total (bottom)?
analogy: 2 out of 5 players found the net — great teamwork!

hint: Would you rather share a cake between 4 people or 8 people?
worked_solution_steps: 1/4 means the cake is cut into 4 pieces.
1/8 means the cake is cut into 8 pieces.
analogy: A quarter of a cake is a nice big slice — an eighth is quite small!
